title: A Minimal Dark $SU(2)$ Origin of a Massless Dirac Neutrino
summary: We propose a gauge-symmetry origin of a rank-two Dirac neutrino mass matrix that enforces one exactly massless neutrino, while being consistent with the oscillation data, as well as cosmological constraints. The mechanism relies on a minimal dark $SU(2)_D$ gauge symmetry under which one right-handed-neutrino-like Weyl fermion is charged, thereby forbidding its Standard Model Yukawa coupling. Quantum consistency then fixes the minimal dark-sector completion: Cancellation of the Witten anomaly requires a second fermionic $SU(2)_D$ doublet, while a discrete $Z_4$ symmetry that forbids Majorana masses allows the two dark doublets to form a vectorlike pair. This anomaly-free completion gives rise to a secluded, confining dark sector with a viable dark matter candidate, linking the protected neutrino texture to dark infrared dynamics.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a gauge-symmetry origin for a rank-two Dirac neutrino mass matrix with one massless neutrino, using a minimal dark SU(2)_D gauge symmetry that forbids a Standard Model Yukawa coupling for a right-handed-neutrino-like Weyl fermion. Quantum consistency via Witten anomaly cancellation and a Z_4 symmetry leads to a confining dark sector with a dark matter candidate, linking the neutrino texture to dark infrared dynamics.
AI.motivation: To explain the origin of a rank-two Dirac neutrino mass matrix that yields one exactly massless neutrino while remaining consistent with oscillation data and cosmological constraints, motivated by the observed neutrino mass hierarchy and the lack of a theoretical symmetry principle for such a texture.
AI.method: The authors introduce a minimal dark SU(2)_D gauge symmetry under which one right-handed-neutrino-like Weyl fermion is charged, forbidding its Standard Model Yukawa coupling. They enforce quantum consistency by requiring cancellation of the Witten anomaly (adding a second SU(2)_D doublet) and impose a discrete Z_4 symmetry to forbid Majorana masses, forming a vectorlike pair of dark doublets. This anomaly-free completion yields a confining dark sector with a viable dark matter candidate.
AI.result: The proposed mechanism naturally produces a rank-two Dirac neutrino mass matrix with exactly one massless neutrino, consistent with oscillation data and cosmological bounds. The dark sector is secluded and confining, providing a dark matter candidate linked to the protected neutrino texture.
AI.conclusion: A gauge-symmetry origin for a rank-two Dirac neutrino mass matrix is viable, with the neutrino texture protected by dark infrared dynamics from a minimal, anomaly-free dark SU(2)_D sector that also accommodates dark matter.

title: Bump Hunting Inside Jets with Energy Correlators
summary: Energy correlators exhibit well-understood scaling behavior in the collinear limit, governed by perturbative QCD dynamics. We explore how this scaling regime is broken by new physics, converting precise energy correlator measurements into a broadband search for new physics. Under generic assumptions, unitarity and positivity are sufficient to classify and constrain the relevant signatures, which imprint an angular resonance on top of this smoothly scaling background. This converts the search into bump hunting within jets. As a proof of principle, we derive projected LHC sensitivity for a light hadrophilic $Z'$, finding competitive constraints with existing searches.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes using energy correlators in jets to search for new physics by looking for angular resonances that break the smooth perturbative QCD scaling behavior. Using unitarity and positivity constraints, they classify new physics signatures and demonstrate sensitivity to a light hadrophilic Z' at the LHC, competitive with existing searches.
AI.motivation: To convert precise energy correlator measurements into a broadband search for new physics by exploiting how the well-understood collinear scaling behavior of QCD is broken by beyond-the-Standard-Model signatures.
AI.method: Unitarity and positivity are used to classify and constrain new physics signatures that imprint an angular resonance on the smoothly scaling QCD background. This recasts the problem as bump hunting within jets.
AI.result: Projected LHC sensitivity for a light hadrophilic Z' yields competitive constraints with existing searches.
AI.conclusion: Energy correlator measurements can serve as a powerful, model-agnostic probe for new physics by detecting angular resonance features that break the expected perturbative QCD scaling.

title: FunKit: A computer algebra toolkit for functional approaches
summary: We introduce FunKit, a Mathematica package for the derivation and tracing of functional equations from arbitrary master equations. FunKit provides an expression vocabulary and a set of rules that allow for derivations in any given field theory and master equation. It also allows users to add extensions for more specific equation systems. Therefore, it can be used in a wide range of situations, for example Dyson--Schwinger or functional RG equations, flowing reparametrisations, nPI equations, (modified) STIs and WTIs, functional Polchinski and Wegner flows, functional master equations with sources, and many others. Besides interfacing with the \FORM language to trace large tensor expressions efficiently, FunKit also provides facilities to export arbitrary Mathematica expressions to C++, Julia or Fortran code, including the results of derivations, which can then be evaluated numerically. Both the tracing and code generation can also be used independently and in combination with other packages.

AI.tldr: FunKit is a Mathematica package that derives and traces functional equations from arbitrary master equations, supporting various field theory formalisms (Dyson-Schwinger, functional RG, nPI, STIs, WTIs, etc.), with efficient tensor tracing via FORM interface and code generation to C++, Julia, or Fortran for numerical evaluation.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified, extensible Mathematica framework for deriving and tracing functional equations from arbitrary master equations across different field theory formalisms, reducing repetitive manual derivations and enabling seamless numerical implementation.
AI.method: The package implements an expression vocabulary and rule set for derivations in any field theory and master equation, with extensible modules for specific equation systems. It interfaces with the FORM language for efficient tensor tracing and provides export facilities to C++, Julia, or Fortran code.
AI.result: FunKit can derive and trace equations for Dyson-Schwinger equations, functional RG equations, flowing reparametrisations, nPI equations, (modified) STIs and WTIs, functional Polchinski/Wegner flows, and functional master equations with sources. Tracing and code generation work independently and with other packages.
AI.conclusion: FunKit is a versatile, extensible tool for functional equation derivations in field theory, bridging analytical derivation and numerical computation through multi-language code generation.

title: Neural Scaling Laws for Jet Generation
summary: Recently observed empirical scaling laws describe the performance of foundation-type models as three independent key quantities -- dataset size, compute, and model parameters -- are modified. Extracting these scaling laws informs the training of large complex models for which the tuning of hyperparameters in traditional ways is not feasible. This work for the first time explores if scaling laws can also be observed for the task of particle jet generation -- both relevant as a pre-training objective for foundation models and as in-situ simulation by itself. We indeed replicate the key logarithmic scaling law behavior for model-size scaling. Beyond studying the next token prediction validation loss of the generative model, we also study the sliced Wasserstein distance of five physical quantities that are not immediately available to the model during training. Our study shows that this quantity is monotonically related to the next token prediction validation loss, meaning that this loss is indeed a good proxy for the physics performance. For the scaling with dataset size and compute, we observe substantially weaker scaling behavior of both the loss and the sliced Wasserstein distance. We analyze this behavior by introducing the concept of a learnable window, and argue that autoregressive next token prediction on jet constituents exhibits comparatively rapid saturation relative to language-model studies. We discuss possible origins of this behavior, including the stochastic nature of QCD radiation and differences between generative and supervised learning tasks in collider physics.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates scaling laws for autoregressive particle jet generation, finding that model-size scaling follows logarithmic patterns similar to foundation models, but dataset size and compute scaling are substantially weaker due to rapid saturation, with the next token prediction loss serving as a good proxy for physics performance.
AI.motivation: To determine if empirical scaling laws (observed for foundation models in relation to dataset size, compute, and model parameters) can also be observed for the task of particle jet generation, which is relevant both as a pre-training objective for foundation models and as in-situ simulation.
AI.method: Study scaling laws for autoregressive next token prediction on particle jet constituents. Analyze validation loss and sliced Wasserstein distance of five physical quantities not directly available during training. Compare scaling behavior across model size, dataset size, and compute. Introduce the concept of a learnable window to analyze saturation effects.
AI.result: Logarithmic scaling law behavior is replicated for model-size scaling. Sliced Wasserstein distance is monotonically related to next token prediction validation loss, confirming the loss as a good proxy for physics performance. Dataset size and compute scaling show substantially weaker behavior, with rapid saturation relative to language-model studies.
AI.conclusion: Autoregressive next token prediction on jet constituents exhibits rapid saturation compared to language models, potentially due to the stochastic nature of QCD radiation and differences between generative and supervised learning tasks in collider physics.

title: Multi-Loop Negative Geometries
summary: Scattering amplitudes in planar ${\cal N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory are dual to expectation values of null polygonal Wilson loops. The Amplituhedron provides a geometric construction for the all-loop integrand as the canonical form on the geometric region in the Grassmannian defined by a certain set of inequalities. For a closely related object, the logarithm of the scattering amplitude, the integrand is reproduced in a similar way using negative geometries. When integrated over all loop momenta except one, the result is infrared (IR) finite and equal to the expectation value of a certain Wilson loop with a Lagrangian insertion. At four points, this quantity, ${\cal F}(g,z)$ only depends on a single cross ratio $z$ and the 't Hooft coupling $g$. At weak coupling, it is known up to three loops from perturbative Wilson loop computations and at strong coupling through the AdS/CFT correspondence at leading order. In this paper, we explore this object further through the lens of the Amplituhedron and negative geometries, which provide very natural IR finite building blocks. We perform an explicit three-loop computation of all negative geometries and show that the number of internal cycles in the diagram is closely linked to the depth of polylogarithms. We calculate the cusp anomalous dimension $Γ_{\rm cusp}$ by integrating ${\cal F}(g,z)$ over $z$. We show that the higher-cycle diagrams are suppressed if we consider separate odd and even zeta contributions. Furthermore, we focus on certain convergent infinite series of one-cycle diagrams, perform all-loop order resummations of such contributions, and discuss various features of the result.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the duality between scattering amplitudes and Wilson loops in planar ${\cal N}=4$ SYM theory using the Amplituhedron and negative geometries. The authors compute all negative geometries at three loops, linking diagram cycles to polylogarithm depth, calculate the cusp anomalous dimension, and perform all-loop resummations of one-cycle diagrams.
AI.motivation: To explore the infrared-finite quantity ${\cal F}(g,z)$ (the integrated form of the logarithm of the scattering amplitude) through the Amplituhedron and negative geometries, providing natural IR-finite building blocks for scattering amplitudes in planar ${\cal N}=4$ SYM.
AI.method: Explicit three-loop computation of all negative geometries; analysis of the connection between internal cycles in diagrams and the depth of polylogarithms; integration of ${\cal F}(g,z)$ to obtain the cusp anomalous dimension; all-loop order resummations of convergent infinite series of one-cycle diagrams.
AI.result: The number of internal cycles in diagrams is closely linked to polylogarithm depth. Higher-cycle diagrams are suppressed when considering separate odd/even zeta contributions. Systematic all-loop resummations of one-cycle diagrams are performed.
AI.conclusion: Negative geometries provide a natural IR-finite framework for studying scattering amplitudes. The cusp anomalous dimension is computed via integration of ${\cal F}(g,z)$. One-cycle diagrams can be resummed to all loops, revealing structural features of the theory.

title: Heavy Axion from a Confining Mirror GUT
summary: We propose a new framework for solving the strong CP problem via a heavy axion, using mirror symmetry and grand unification. The mirror GUT sector remains unbroken and dynamically generates a calculable heavy mass scale via confinement without fine tuning. Models in this class feature a heavy axion, whose potential is less sensitive to Planck scale corrections, as well as a rich hidden sector from the confined mirror GUT. The solution to the strong CP problem remains unspoiled by the presence of additional phases in the GUT Yukawas, yet allowing the possibility of electric dipole moments within the reach of future experiments. Our proposal offers new directions in GUT model building, axion phenomenology, dark matter and cosmology.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes solving the strong CP problem using a heavy axion in a mirror GUT framework where confinement dynamically generates a heavy mass scale without fine-tuning, with testable EDMs and rich hidden sector phenomenology.
AI.motivation: To solve the strong CP problem via a heavy axion mechanism that avoids fine-tuning and Planck-scale sensitivity, while remaining compatible with grand unification and allowing testable EDM signatures.
AI.method: The framework combines mirror symmetry with grand unification; the mirror GUT sector remains unbroken and dynamically generates a calculable heavy mass scale via confinement, producing a heavy axion whose potential is less sensitive to Planck-scale corrections.
AI.result: The solution preserves the strong CP problem solution despite additional CP phases in GUT Yukawas, while enabling EDMs within reach of future experiments; the confined mirror GUT yields a rich hidden sector.
AI.conclusion: This approach opens new directions for GUT model building, axion phenomenology, dark matter, and cosmology by offering a UV-complete heavy axion solution to the strong CP problem.

title: Analytic Bootstrap for $O(N)$ Boundary Conformal Field Theories with Interacting Boundaries
summary: We investigate $O(N)$ boundary conformal field theories (BCFTs) with boundary interactions in $d=4-ε$ and $d=3-ε$ employing the analytic bootstrap. By deriving universal constraints on conformal data, we show that infinitely many operator expansions can be expressed in terms of a finite set of inputs. Complementing the analytic bootstrap with a perturbative renormalization-group analysis, we identify totally new boundary fixed points in $d=4-ε$, including non-unitary ones, generated by a boundary cubic coupling, and compute their conformal data to leading order. Moreover, we leverage our solution in $d=3-ε$ to extract, for the first time, the boundary conformal data for the tricritical $O(N)$ model. Altogether, our approach provides a unified prescription for BCFTs with interacting boundaries and streamlines the determination of bulk and boundary operator expansions.

AI.tldr: The paper studies O(N) boundary conformal field theories in d=4-ε and d=3-ε using analytic bootstrap and perturbative RG, discovering new boundary fixed points (including non-unitary ones) and computing boundary conformal data for the tricritical O(N) model for the first time.
AI.motivation: To derive universal constraints on conformal data in O(N) BCFTs with boundary interactions, enabling a streamlined determination of operator expansions and identification of new boundary fixed points.
AI.method: Combines analytic bootstrap (deriving universal constraints showing infinitely many operator expansions reduce to a finite set of inputs) with perturbative renormalization-group analysis in both d=4-ε and d=3-ε dimensions.
AI.result: Identified totally new boundary fixed points in d=4-ε (including non-unitary ones) generated by a boundary cubic coupling, computed their leading-order conformal data; extracted for the first time the boundary conformal data for the tricritical O(N) model in d=3-ε.
AI.conclusion: The approach provides a unified prescription for BCFTs with interacting boundaries and streamlines the determination of both bulk and boundary operator expansions.

title: Twilight of the WIMP: Comprehensive Phenomenology of Electroweak Triplet Dark Matter
summary: We present a comprehensive study of dark matter phenomenology in standard model extensions featuring an electroweak triplet scalar or fermion with hypercharge $Y = 0$ or $Y = 2$. These minimal triplet extensions provide well-motivated dark matter candidates stabilised by the $Z_2$ discrete symmetry. We perform a detailed analysis of the parameter space consistent with current cosmological and experimental constraints, including the relic abundance, direct detection limits, and indirect detection bounds. We find that the scalar triplet with $Y=0$ is ruled out by a combination of relic density, direct detection and indirect detection constraints. On the other hand, the scalar and fermionic triplets with $Y=2$ are both excluded by current direct detection experiments due to their large spin-independent scattering cross-sections. The viable parameter space of the remaining $Y=0$ fermion triplet dark matter lies within the projected sensitivity of near-future experiments, particularly those targeting indirect detection signatures. Collider prospects for these triplet extensions are also discussed in the Appendix.

AI.tldr: A study of dark matter candidates in electroweak triplet extensions (scalar/fermion, Y=0 or Y=2) constrained by relic abundance, direct/indirect detection, and collider data. The Y=0 scalar triplet is ruled out; Y=2 scalar and fermion triplets are excluded by direct detection; only the Y=0 fermion triplet remains viable, within reach of future experiments.
AI.motivation: To systematically assess the viability of electroweak triplet extensions (scalar and fermion with Y=0 or Y=2) as dark matter candidates under current cosmological and experimental constraints, identifying which models survive and where future searches are most promising.
AI.method: Parameter space scans constrained by observed relic abundance, direct detection limits (spin-independent scattering cross-sections), indirect detection bounds, and collider prospects. The dark matter candidates are stabilized by a Z₂ discrete symmetry.
AI.result: The scalar triplet with Y=0 is excluded by combined relic density, direct detection, and indirect detection constraints. Scalar and fermionic triplets with Y=2 are excluded by direct detection due to large spin-independent cross-sections. Only the Y=0 fermion triplet remains viable.
AI.conclusion: The viable Y=0 fermion triplet dark matter lies within the projected sensitivity of near-future experiments, especially indirect detection. Collider prospects are discussed in the appendix. No currently viable triplet scenarios remain unconstrained except the Y=0 fermion case.

title: Gravity Decoupling and Axionic Shift Symmetries
summary: We analyse the rôle of approximate axionic shift symmetries in gravity-decoupling limits arising in type II Calabi-Yau compactifications. Associated with each shift symmetry there is an axionic string whose tension constrains the gradient of the Kähler potential, as expected in regimes where gravity becomes weakly coupled. The gradients of these tensions define vector fields on moduli space, analogous to those associated with BPS particle masses. Together, they characterise the evolution of different effective field theory sectors along asymptotic limits, encoding both their coupling to gravity and their kinetic mixing. By deriving upper bounds on the inner products of these vector fields, we show that they split into mutually orthogonal subsets, one of which decouples from gravity. Finally, we relate the Laplacian of certain axionic string tensions to a divergent moduli space curvature.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes approximate axionic shift symmetries in gravity-decoupling limits of type II Calabi-Yau compactifications, showing that axionic string tensions constrain Kähler potential gradients, define vector fields on moduli space similar to BPS particle masses, and split into orthogonal subsets where one decouples from gravity.
AI.motivation: To understand the role of axionic shift symmetries and their associated strings in gravity-decoupling limits arising from Calabi-Yau compactifications.
AI.method: Analysis of axionic string tensions as constraints on Kähler potential gradients, definition of vector fields on moduli space analogous to BPS particle masses, derivation of upper bounds on inner products of these vector fields.
AI.result: Vector fields split into mutually orthogonal subsets, one of which decouples from gravity. The Laplacian of certain axionic string tensions relates to divergent moduli space curvature.
AI.conclusion: The evolution of effective field theory sectors along asymptotic limits is characterized by the gradients of axionic string tensions, encoding both gravitational coupling and kinetic mixing.

title: Visible inelasticity as a probe of tau flavor content of astrophysical neutrinos
summary: Astrophysical neutrinos provide a unique probe of neutrino flavor changes over cosmological baselines. While the tau component of the neutrino flux is expected to arise almost entirely from mixing, current measurements rely primarily on rare double-cascade signatures. We investigate a complementary method to measure the tau fraction using the visible inelasticity of starting track events in neutrino telescopes. Muonic decays of tau leptons produce tracks with systematically larger visible inelasticity than those from muon neutrino interactions, potentially enabling statistical separation of the two flavors. Using realistic IceCube exposures and detector performance, we show that this observable already yields competitive sensitivity to the tau-to-muon flux ratio, $R_{τμ}$, achievable with existing data. This approach may further enable flavor measurements of individual sources and the selection of tau-enhanced source catalogs. Starting-track inelasticity thus provides a powerful and immediately accessible probe of astrophysical neutrino flavor and of potential physics beyond standard neutrino mixing.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes using visible inelasticity of starting track events in neutrino telescopes (like IceCube) to measure the tau-to-muon flux ratio of astrophysical neutrinos, offering a complementary approach to rare double-cascade signatures. This method provides competitive sensitivity with existing data and enables flavor measurements of individual sources.
AI.motivation: Astrophysical neutrinos probe neutrino flavor changes over cosmological baselines, but current tau component measurements rely on rare double-cascade signatures, limiting sensitivity and source-specific flavor studies.
AI.method: The authors investigate using visible inelasticity of starting track events to statistically separate tau and muon neutrino interactions, leveraging the fact that muonic decays of tau leptons produce tracks with systematically larger visible inelasticity than muon neutrino interactions.
AI.result: Using realistic IceCube exposures and detector performance, the approach yields competitive sensitivity to the tau-to-muon flux ratio (R_{τμ}) achievable with existing data.
AI.conclusion: Starting-track inelasticity provides a powerful and immediately accessible probe of astrophysical neutrino flavor and potential physics beyond standard neutrino mixing, enabling flavor measurements of individual sources and tau-enhanced source catalog selection.

title: Dynamical Entanglement Phase Transitions in Holographic CFTs
summary: We study the time evolution of the entanglement structure of holographic conformal field theories after a local quench. Using the mutual information between two spatial intervals as a probe, we find that $1+1$-dimensional conformal field theories exhibit a rich pattern of dynamical phase transitions. In the large-central-charge limit, mutual information develops sharp non-analyticities at critical times, providing a concrete entanglement-based realization of dynamical quantum phase transitions. We find that the dynamics organize into six distinct phases of mutual information, each controlled by the dominance of a different conformal block, or equivalently, a different holographic geodesic configuration. This phase structure goes beyond the standard quasi-particle picture, explaining non-analytic features that are not captured by simple light-cone propagation from the quench points. We further identify a dynamical $D_4$ symmetry acting on the interval endpoints that controls the presence or absence of mutual information. The onset of mutual information is governed by the breaking of this symmetry to a $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2$ subgroup, suggesting a symmetry-based characterization of non-equilibrium entanglement dynamics analogous to the role of symmetry in equilibrium critical phenomena. Finally, numerical studies of critical spin chains indicate that finite-$c$ effects smooth out the sharp large-$c$ transitions between different mutual-information phases, while the transitions between phases with and without mutual information appear to remain non-analytic. These results offer a unifying perspective on real-time entanglement dynamics and their critical features in conformal many-body systems.

AI.tldr: This paper studies entanglement dynamics after a local quench in holographic CFTs, revealing six phases of mutual information governed by conformal block dominance and a dynamical D4 symmetry, with sharp non-analyticities at large central charge that are smoothed by finite-c effects except for transitions between phases with/without mutual information.
AI.motivation: To understand the real-time entanglement dynamics and their critical features in conformal many-body systems, particularly the rich pattern of dynamical phase transitions in mutual information after a local quench, going beyond the standard quasi-particle picture.
AI.method: Studying mutual information between two spatial intervals in 1+1D holographic CFTs after a local quench, using large-central-charge limits (holographic dual), conformal block analysis, holographic geodesic configurations, dynamical D4 symmetry analysis, and numerical studies of critical spin chains for finite-c effects.
AI.result: Identified six distinct phases of mutual information dynamics, each controlled by dominance of different conformal blocks/geodesic configurations. Discovered a dynamical D4 symmetry whose breaking to Z2×Z2 governs onset of mutual information. Finite-c effects smooth sharp transitions except for transitions between phases with/without mutual information.
AI.conclusion: The entanglement dynamics after local quenches exhibit a rich phase structure with symmetry-based characterization of non-equilibrium entanglement dynamics, offering a unifying perspective on real-time entanglement dynamics and their critical features in conformal many-body systems.

title: Dynamical Tsallis WIMP Freeze-Out and Residual Memory Channels in the Radiation Sector
summary: In this work we generalize the thermal decoupling, or freeze-out, of weakly interacting massive particle dark matter within the Tsallis nonextensive formalism. The generalization is implemented through $q$-deformed distribution functions obtained from the maximum entropy principle with Curado-Tsallis constraints. The Tsallis parameter $q$, which measures deviations from extensivity with respect to the limit $q=1$, is promoted to a dynamical quantity depending on the dimensionless variable $x=m_χ/T$, where $m_χ$ is the dark matter mass. This dynamical evolution is characterized by a relaxation toward extensivity, while requiring that the nonextensive deformation is not completely erased before freeze-out. We solve the Boltzmann equation assuming a sectorial deformation, where only the dark matter equilibrium abundance is generalized and the radiation background remains extensive. The relic abundance is computed for different dark matter masses and initial values of the Tsallis parameter. From this evolution, we extract the residual value $q_χ^{\rm fo}$ at freeze-out, which is then used as the initial input for a phenomenological memory channel. This channel propagates the residual nonextensivity into the radiation sector, specifically into the electron-positron plasma and neutrinos, while photons are kept extensive in order to avoid direct tensions with CMB physics. The resulting deformation modifies the neutrino energy density and the photon reheating contribution, producing a correction to $N_{\rm eff}$. We compare the predicted values with the compressed CMB+BAO constraint on $N_{\rm eff}$ and find that the residual-memory scenario can remain phenomenologically compatible with current bounds.

AI.tldr: The paper generalizes WIMP dark matter freeze-out using Tsallis nonextensive statistics with a dynamical q-parameter that relaxes toward extensivity. It computes relic abundances and shows that residual nonextensivity can propagate to the radiation sector, producing corrections to N_eff that remain compatible with CMB+BAO constraints.
AI.motivation: To extend the standard WIMP thermal decoupling framework by incorporating nonextensive (Tsallis) statistics, motivated by the possibility that dark matter may deviate from standard Maxwell-Boltzmann statistics, and to test phenomenological consequences in cosmic observables like N_eff.
AI.method: The authors use q-deformed distribution functions from maximum entropy with Curado-Tsallis constraints, promote q to a dynamical function of x=m_χ/T, solve the Boltzmann equation with sectorial deformation (only dark matter generalized), and develop a residual-memory channel that propagates nonextensivity into e⁺e⁻ plasma and neutrinos while keeping photons extensive.
AI.result: The relic abundance is computed for various dark matter masses and initial q values. The residual q at freeze-out is extracted and used to compute N_eff corrections. The predicted N_eff values remain compatible with compressed CMB+BAO constraints.
AI.conclusion: The Tsallis nonextensive generalization of WIMP freeze-out, with dynamical q relaxation and a residual-memory channel into the radiation sector, is phenomenologically viable within current cosmological bounds on N_eff.

title: Constrained integrability and anyonic chains
summary: We review the notion of Yang-Baxter integrability for spin chains that have Hilbert spaces with constraints, such as a Rydberg blockade. We focus on anyonic chains, whose constraints arise from the fusion rules of the fusion categories on which they are based. We discuss the emergence of Temperley-Lieb algebras and present a new result on which types of anyonic chains exhibit them. We then give an overview of known results for integrable anyonic chains and extend them to several fusion categories up to rank $7$. Using a modification of the boost operator formalism, we find several new integrable anyonic chains and discuss some of their properties. These include spin-$\frac32$ models for $\mathfrak{su}(2)_k$ fusion categories, anyonic chains based on the Tambara-Yamagami fusion categories TY$(\mathbb{Z}_n)$, and product fusion categories Fib$\times$Fib and Fib$\times$Ising. We review recent results for spin chains based on the Haagerup-Izumi fusion category HI$(\mathbb{Z}_3)$, and present preliminary numerics for a HI$(\mathbb{Z}_5)$ model.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews Yang-Baxter integrability for constrained spin chains (e.g., anyonic chains with Rydberg blockade-like constraints), derives conditions for Temperley-Lieb algebra emergence, and discovers new integrable anyonic chains across several fusion categories up to rank 7 using a modified boost operator formalism. New models include spin-3/2 su(2)_k chains, Tambara-Yamagami TY(Z_n) chains, product categories Fib×Fib and Fib×Ising, and preliminary numerics for HI(Z_5).
AI.motivation: To systematically study and extend Yang-Baxter integrability to spin chains with constrained Hilbert spaces (e.g., Rydberg blockade) by leveraging the algebraic structure of fusion categories and anyonic chains, and to discover new integrable models beyond known ones.
AI.method: Review of fusion category formalism for anyonic chains; analysis of Temperley-Lieb algebra emergence conditions in anyonic chains; application of a modified boost operator formalism to systematically search for integrable Hamiltonians across fusion categories up to rank 7.
AI.result: New integrable anyonic chains discovered: spin-3/2 models for su(2)_k, chains based on Tambara-Yamagami TY(Z_n) categories, product categories Fib×Fib and Fib×Ising. Preliminary numerics for HI(Z_5) presented. Conditions for Temperley-Lieb algebra emergence clarified for various fusion categories.
AI.conclusion: The boost operator approach is effective for finding new integrable anyonic chains. A rich landscape of integrable models exists across fusion categories, with potential applications to constrained quantum systems like Rydberg atom arrays.

title: Hiding in the Shadow of the Upsilon: Ditaus from a Light Pseudoscalar
summary: The CMS collaboration has reported a measurement of $Υ$ decays to ditaus using $61.9~{\rm fb}^{-1}$ of scouting data. If interpreted as the decay of $Υ(1S,2S,3S)$, the measured ditau rate is more than ten times that seen in the dimuon final states at the $\sim 3 σ$ level, and is likewise inconsistent with the branching ratios measured at $B$-factories. If confirmed with more data and at higher significance, such a violation of lepton flavor universality would necessitate new physics. In this Letter, we present a simple model with a light pseudoscalar coincidentally near the $Υ(1S)$ mass, which mixes with two Higgs doublets in the alignment limit. Such a particle naturally decays primarily to taus and evades all existing experimental constraints, while implying a number of predictions that can be tested in the near future.

AI.tldr: The CMS collaboration found a potential excess in Υ decays to ditaus compared to dimuons, suggesting lepton flavor universality violation. The authors propose a light pseudoscalar near the Υ(1S) mass mixing with Higgs doublets as a possible explanation, which decays mainly to taus and avoids current constraints.
AI.motivation: To explain the CMS observation of an anomalously high ditau rate from Υ decays (∼3σ excess over dimuon rates and B-factory measurements), which would indicate lepton flavor universality violation requiring new physics if confirmed.
AI.method: The authors construct a model featuring a light pseudoscalar particle with mass coincidentally near the Υ(1S) mass, which mixes with two Higgs doublets in the alignment limit. This particle is designed to decay predominantly to tau leptons.
AI.result: The proposed light pseudoscalar model can account for the observed ditau excess while evading all existing experimental constraints, and yields several testable predictions.
AI.conclusion: If the CMS ditau excess is confirmed at higher significance, the light pseudoscalar model offers a viable new physics explanation that predicts specific observable signatures testable in the near future.

title: Bootstrapping the Four-Point NMHV Stress-Tensor Form Factor
comment: 5 + 4 pages, 3 figures and 1 table, ancillary files included
summary: We bootstrap the two-loop four-point next-to-maximally helicity-violating (NMHV) ratio function for the chiral stress-tensor form factor in planar maximally supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory (sYM) at the symbol level. Starting from an ansatz built from NMHV leading singularities and the known two-loop five-point one-mass integral function space, we impose finiteness, dihedral symmetry, parity and Galois symmetry, spurious-pole cancellation, collinear limits, and finally triple-collinear consistency, which together fix the result uniquely. We then subject the answer to independent soft and double-soft checks. The resulting symbol contains 78 letters, all drawn from the 88-letter alphabet previously identified for the four-point MHV form factor through four loops. This provides the first multi-loop result for a non-MHV form factor, and direct evidence that the 88-letter alphabet extends beyond the MHV sector, which may provide the natural universal alphabet for four-point form factors. Our result supplies new data for the study of physics and mathematics of multi-loop form factors including the antipodal duality, as well as their relations to Higgs-parton amplitudes in QCD.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first multi-loop (two-loop, four-point) NMHV form factor result in planar N=4 sYM, derived via a bootstrap approach using an ansatz from leading singularities and known integral functions, imposing multiple physical constraints. The resulting symbol uses 78 letters from a known 88-letter alphabet, showing its universality beyond MHV.
AI.motivation: To extend the bootstrap program for form factors beyond the MHV sector to NMHV level, providing the first multi-loop non-MHV form factor result and testing whether the known 88-letter alphabet for MHV form factors is universal for all helicity sectors.
AI.method: Symbol bootstrap: build ansatz from NMHV leading singularities and two-loop five-point one-mass integral function space; impose finiteness, dihedral symmetry, parity, Galois symmetry, spurious-pole cancellation, collinear limits, and triple-collinear consistency; then verify with soft and double-soft checks.
AI.result: Uniquely determined two-loop four-point NMHV form factor symbol containing 78 letters from the 88-letter alphabet previously identified for the four-point MHV form factor through four loops.
AI.conclusion: The 88-letter alphabet is universal beyond the MHV sector for four-point form factors; this result provides new data for studying antipodal duality and relations to Higgs-parton amplitudes in QCD.

title: Alignment and Enhanced Multi-Higgs Production
summary: Contrary to conventional expectations, we identify a class of extended scalar-sector scenarios in which final states with two, three, or four Higgs bosons constitute the leading discovery channels for new physics at the LHC. In these scenarios, higher-dimensional interactions, together with suppressed Higgs-scalar mixing near the alignment limit, reorganize the decay patterns of new scalar states, suppressing conventional modes while enhancing multi-Higgs final states. We illustrate the emergence of dominant triple- and quadruple-Higgs signatures in two representative realizations: a single-scalar extension of the Standard Model, where higher-dimensional operators suppress conventional two-body decays while preserving couplings to higher-multiplicity Higgs final states; and a two-singlet scenario, where similar signatures arise through cascade decays with a simpler operator structure. In both cases, the new scalar states can be produced via gluon fusion, yielding potentially observable rates for multi-Higgs production at the LHC. Although both realizations lead to identical final states, they exhibit distinct kinematic features reflecting their underlying topologies, providing a direct handle on the dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies scalar-sector scenarios where multi-Higgs (2, 3, or 4) final states become the leading discovery channels for new physics at the LHC, due to higher-dimensional interactions and suppressed Higgs-scalar mixing. Two realizations are studied: a single-scalar extension and a two-singlet scenario, both producing observable multi-Higgs rates via gluon fusion with distinct kinematic features.
AI.motivation: Conventional searches for new physics often focus on single-Higgs or diboson final states. This paper challenges that expectation by identifying scenarios where multi-Higgs final states are the dominant discovery channels.
AI.method: The authors study two representative realizations: (1) a single-scalar extension with higher-dimensional operators suppressing two-body decays while enhancing multi-Higgs final states, and (2) a two-singlet scenario producing similar signatures via cascade decays with a simpler operator structure. Both are analyzed in the alignment limit with suppressed Higgs-scalar mixing.
AI.result: Both scenarios lead to dominant triple- and quadruple-Higgs signatures with potentially observable rates at the LHC via gluon fusion. Despite identical final states, the two realizations exhibit distinct kinematic features reflecting their different underlying topologies.
AI.conclusion: Multi-Higgs final states can serve as leading discovery channels for new physics at the LHC in extended scalar-sector scenarios, and kinematic differences between realizations provide a handle to distinguish the underlying dynamics.

title: Quantum State of a Gravitating Region
summary: We propose that any compact $d$-manifold with elliptic data, $\mathcal{J}$, prepares a quantum state $|\mathcal{J}\rangle$ on its $(d-1)$-boundary $σ$. Elliptic data consists of metric and field values, or their conjugates, but not both. No asymptotic structure is required. Inner products and traces are evaluated by the gravitational path integral with closed boundary conditions obtained by gluing elliptic data manifolds. In particular, we give a prescription for the Rényi entropies $S_n$ of a subregion of $σ$. In a class of examples, we find that $S_n$ is nonnegative and nonincreasing with $n$, as required for consistency. We obtain the von Neumann entropy by analytic continuation and find agreement with the minimal surface prescription of Bousso and Penington.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes that any compact d-manifold with elliptic data (metric and field values, but not conjugates) prepares a quantum state on its (d-1)-boundary. Inner products and traces are evaluated via gravitational path integrals with closed boundary conditions from gluing elliptic data manifolds. A prescription for Rényi entropies of a subregion is given, shown to be nonnegative and nonincreasing with n, and the von Neumann entropy from analytic continuation agrees with the Bousso-Penington minimal surface prescription.
AI.motivation: To develop a covariant prescription for preparing quantum states and computing entanglement entropies in quantum gravity without requiring asymptotic structure, extending the island formula and replica trick to more general settings.
AI.method: The method defines quantum states via compact manifolds with elliptic data (elliptic boundary conditions specifying either metric/field values or their conjugates). Inner products and traces are computed by gluing such manifolds and evaluating the gravitational path integral. Rényi entropies are computed via replicated geometries with closed boundary conditions, and analytic continuation yields the von Neumann entropy.
AI.result: Rényi entropies S_n for a subregion are found to be nonnegative and nonincreasing with n, consistent with quantum information requirements. Analytic continuation to n=1 reproduces the von Neumann entropy matching the Bousso-Penington minimal surface prescription.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a general covariant method for state preparation and entropy computation in quantum gravity using elliptic data, without relying on asymptotic boundaries, and validates consistency with known minimal surface results.

title: High-Quality Axion Dark Matter without Isocurvature Problem
summary: Axion dark matter in high-scale inflation is subject to the isocurvature constraint, since quantum fluctuations of the axion field during inflation may exceed the current CMB bound. One conventional way to suppress these fluctuations is to assume that the Peccei-Quinn field has a large expectation value during inflation. However, this mechanism becomes ineffective when the axion domain wall number is large. In this work, we point out that a high-quality axion protected by a discrete gauge symmetry can naturally evade this problem. A Peccei-Quinn-violating but gauge-invariant operator induces a large effective axion mass during inflation, thereby suppressing the axion fluctuation. The same setup can address both the axion quality problem and the isocurvature problem, while leading to a prediction for the axion parameter space to be verified in future experiments.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes that a high-quality axion protected by a discrete gauge symmetry can simultaneously solve the axion quality problem and the isocurvature problem in high-scale inflation. A PQ-violating but gauge-invariant operator generates a large effective axion mass during inflation, suppressing quantum fluctuations that would otherwise exceed CMB bounds.
AI.motivation: To address the isocurvature constraint on axion dark matter in high-scale inflation, which arises because quantum fluctuations of the axion field during inflation may exceed current CMB bounds. The conventional solution (large PQ field expectation value) fails when the axion domain wall number is large.
AI.method: The authors introduce a PQ-violating but gauge-invariant operator that induces a large effective axion mass during inflation, suppressing axion fluctuations. This is combined with a discrete gauge symmetry to protect the axion quality.
AI.result: The setup can suppress axion quantum fluctuations during inflation, evading the isocurvature constraint, while simultaneously addressing the axion quality problem. It leads to a prediction for the axion parameter space testable in future experiments.
AI.conclusion: A high-quality axion with discrete gauge symmetry provides a natural solution to both the isocurvature and quality problems, producing a testable parameter space prediction.

title: Asymptotic Quantum Dynamics of Ghost Fields
summary: The dressed propagator of a ghost coupled to ordinary fields develops a pair of complex conjugate poles in the first Riemann sheet above the multi-particle threshold. We study the implications of this pole structure for the asymptotic field and its negative-norm one-particle state. Within the operator formalism of local quantum field theory, we show that interactions between the ghost field and the composite field of the multi-particle state persist at asymptotic times. These induce quantum interference effects that render the negative-norm one-particle state non-orthogonal to, and thus indistinguishable from, a superposition of positive-norm multi-particle states. As a result, no free asymptotic one-particle ghost state exists. The real and imaginary parts of the complex mass admit a clear physical interpretation; in particular, the inverse imaginary part sets the timescale for the onset of non-orthogonality. A freely propagating ghost is therefore confined to time intervals much shorter than its inverse width, so that a detector can never observe an isolated ghost particle asymptotically. Open questions and potential applications are discussed in the conclusions.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that ghost particles with complex conjugate poles in their dressed propagator cannot exist as free asymptotic one-particle states because interactions with multi-particle states cause quantum interference, making the negative-norm ghost state indistinguishable from positive-norm multi-particle states; the inverse imaginary mass sets the confinement timescale.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical implications of complex conjugate poles appearing in the dressed propagator of a ghost field coupled to ordinary fields, particularly regarding the existence and observability of asymptotic ghost one-particle states.
AI.method: Using the operator formalism of local quantum field theory, the authors analyze the asymptotic behavior of the ghost field and its negative-norm one-particle state, examining interactions between the ghost field and composite multi-particle state fields at asymptotic times.
AI.result: The negative-norm one-particle ghost state becomes non-orthogonal to and indistinguishable from a superposition of positive-norm multi-particle states due to quantum interference. No free asymptotic one-particle ghost state exists. The inverse imaginary part of the complex mass sets the timescale for onset of non-orthogonality.
AI.conclusion: Ghost particles are confined to time intervals much shorter than their inverse width, preventing asymptotic observation. The complex mass parameters have clear physical interpretations, and freely propagating ghosts cannot be detected in isolation.

title: Charmonium production at SPS and FAIR energies
summary: In this study we apply the Remler formalism to charmonium production at SPS and GSI/FAIR energies in order to investigate the effects of baryon-rich matter on charmonium production and dissociation in heavy-ion collisions within the Parton-Hadron-String Dynamics (PHSD). As a first step the Remler formalism is tested in p+p collisions and then applied to p+A collisions in order to extract the nuclear absorption cross section of charmonium, which is then utilized in heavy-ion collisions. We find that the Remler formalism successfully describes charmonium production in heavy-ion collisions at SPS energies when an in-medium heavy quark potential is implemented, in which $J/ψ$ dissociates near $T_c$. Finally the same formalism is applied to the GSI/FAIR energies, where we estimate charmonium production.

AI.tldr: This study applies the Remler formalism to charmonium production in heavy-ion collisions at SPS and GSI/FAIR energies using the PHSD model, incorporating an in-medium heavy quark potential where J/ψ dissociates near T_c. The formalism successfully describes charmonium production at SPS energies and provides estimates for GSI/FAIR energies.
AI.motivation: To investigate the effects of baryon-rich matter on charmonium production and dissociation in heavy-ion collisions, and to test the applicability of the Remler formalism in this context.
AI.method: The Remler formalism is implemented within the Parton-Hadron-String Dynamics (PHSD) model. It is first tested in p+p collisions, then applied to p+A collisions to extract the nuclear absorption cross section of charmonium, and finally used in heavy-ion collisions with an in-medium heavy quark potential.
AI.result: The Remler formalism successfully describes charmonium production in heavy-ion collisions at SPS energies when an in-medium heavy quark potential is implemented, with J/ψ dissociation occurring near T_c. Production estimates are also provided for GSI/FAIR energies.
AI.conclusion: The Remler formalism is a viable approach for modeling charmonium production in baryon-rich heavy-ion collisions, and its application at GSI/FAIR energies provides useful predictions for future experiments.

title: Asymptotically Safe Gravitational Form Factors from the Proper-Time Flow Equation
summary: We study the renormalization group flow of non-local form factors in four-dimensional quantum gravity within the proper-time formalism at quadratic order in the curvature expansion. We show that the flow equations can be integrated down to $k=0$, allowing the reconstruction of the full momentum dependence of the form factors. Within this framework, we construct asymptotically safe solutions at this order. We find that asymptotic safety of the flow does not automatically ensure a finite cutoff-independent $Λ\to\infty$ limit for the integrated solutions, which in general develop a logarithmic divergence $\ln(q^2/Λ^2)$, so that a renormalization condition is still required. A finite $Λ\to\infty$ limit compatible with asymptotic safety is obtained only when the ultraviolet boundary condition selects the non-Gaussian fixed point. This yields finite dimensionful form factors, removes UV logarithmic contributions, and ensures independence from the renormalization scale $μ$. The resulting renormalized asymptotically safe form factors display a power-law decay $\sim1/q^2$ in the ultraviolet and reproduce the expected logarithmic structure in the infrared, with the Planck scale replacing the renormalization scale.

AI.tldr: This paper studies non-local form factors in quantum gravity using proper-time formalism, showing that asymptotic safety at quadratic order requires specific UV boundary conditions (the non-Gaussian fixed point) to yield finite, cutoff-independent form factors that decay as 1/q² in the UV and have logarithmic IR structure.
AI.motivation: To understand the renormalization group flow and momentum dependence of non-local form factors in quantum gravity within the asymptotic safety scenario, and to determine whether asymptotic safety alone guarantees a consistent UV limit.
AI.method: Proper-time formalism with renormalization group flow equations at quadratic order in curvature expansion, integrated down to k=0 to reconstruct full momentum dependence of form factors.
AI.result: Asymptotic safety does not automatically ensure a finite Λ→∞ limit; a logarithmic divergence ln(q²/Λ²) appears unless the UV boundary condition selects the non-Gaussian fixed point. Only then are form factors finite, UV log-free, μ-independent, decaying as ~1/q² in the UV with logarithmic IR structure and Planck scale replacing the renormalization scale.
AI.conclusion: A renormalization condition is still required in asymptotically safe quantum gravity; the non-Gaussian fixed point must be imposed as the UV boundary condition to obtain well-defined, cutoff-independent renormalized form factors.

title: Polyakov-loop potential of accelerated gluonic matter and subtlety in thermodynamics
summary: We study the one-loop Polyakov-loop effective potential in pure gluonic matter under constant acceleration. We perform the computation in both the Euclidean Rindler spacetime and the optical spacetime, which are related via a conformal transformation. The results from the two formulations correspond to physically different observables, and we clarify their connection to specific components of the energy-momentum tensor. This identification resolves a discrepancy previously noted for fields on conical backgrounds. For the Polyakov-loop expectation value, we should minimize the effective potential computed in the optical metric formulation, which concludes that real acceleration strengthens deconfining properties. We also discuss analytic continuation from real to imaginary acceleration and find a perturbatively confined phase. We point out some suggestive similarities and differences between systems under imaginary acceleration and imaginary rotation.

AI.tldr: The paper studies the one-loop Polyakov-loop effective potential in pure gluonic matter under constant acceleration, using both Euclidean Rindler spacetime and optical spacetime formulations. It resolves discrepancies in earlier work on conical backgrounds, shows that real acceleration strengthens deconfinement, and explores imaginary acceleration to find a perturbatively confined phase, drawing comparisons with imaginary rotation.
AI.motivation: To understand how constant acceleration affects the confining/deconfining properties of pure gluonic matter, and to resolve a previously noted discrepancy in the Polyakov-loop effective potential computed on conical backgrounds.
AI.method: The authors compute the one-loop Polyakov-loop effective potential in both Euclidean Rindler spacetime and the conformally related optical spacetime, and clarify the connection between the two formulations via specific components of the energy-momentum tensor.
AI.result: Real acceleration strengthens deconfining properties (lowers the critical temperature). Imaginary acceleration leads to a perturbatively confined phase. The discrepancy for fields on conical backgrounds is resolved by properly identifying which observable corresponds to which formulation.
AI.conclusion: The optical metric formulation should be used for the Polyakov-loop expectation value, showing acceleration enhances deconfinement. Imaginary acceleration yields a confined phase, with suggestive similarities and differences compared to imaginary rotation.

title: Higher Wess-Zumino-Witten term from semistrict higher Chern-Simons theory
summary: We show that in any $2n+2$ dimensions, the higher Chern-Simons action built from a semistrict Lie 2-algebra gives a non-trivial higher Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) term under a higher gauge transformation. The key point is that the non-zero Jacobiator directly generates the higher WZW term, hereas it vanishes when reduced to the strict case.

AI.tldr: In 2n+2 dimensions, a higher Chern-Simons action from a semistrict Lie 2-algebra produces a nontrivial higher Wess-Zumino-Witten term via higher gauge transformations, with the non-zero Jacobiator being the direct source.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that a non-zero Jacobiator in semistrict Lie 2-algebras generates nontrivial higher WZW terms, unlike the strict case where it vanishes.
AI.method: The authors analyze higher Chern-Simons actions built from semistrict Lie 2-algebras in 2n+2 dimensions and examine the effect of higher gauge transformations on the generation of higher WZW terms.
AI.result: A non-trivial higher WZW term is produced under higher gauge transformations when the Jacobiator is non-zero, whereas it vanishes in the strict Lie 2-algebra case.
AI.conclusion: Higher gauge transformations of the higher Chern-Simons action in semistrict settings yield nontrivial higher WZW terms directly from the non-zero Jacobiator.

title: Quantum field theory of massive chiral fields
summary: We present a quantum-field-theoretic treatment of massive chiral fields in which particles possess well-defined chirality and helicity. This framework reproduces the chiral oscillation formula previously obtained in first-quantized approaches and provides a consistent description of weak-interaction processes. We further derive corresponding chiral-energy uncertainty relations.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a quantum-field-theoretic treatment of massive chiral fields, showing well-defined chirality and helicity for particles, reproducing chiral oscillation formulas, and deriving chiral-energy uncertainty relations.
AI.motivation: To provide a consistent quantum-field-theoretic foundation for massive chiral fields, overcoming limitations of first-quantized approaches and establishing a rigorous framework for chiral oscillations and weak-interaction processes.
AI.method: Quantum field theory treatment of massive chiral fields, analyzing chirality and helicity properties, reproducing chiral oscillation formulas, and deriving uncertainty relations.
AI.result: Successful reproduction of chiral oscillation formulas from first-quantized approaches within a QFT framework, and derivation of chiral-energy uncertainty relations.
AI.conclusion: The QFT framework provides a consistent description of massive chiral fields with well-defined chirality/helicity, valid for weak-interaction processes, and introduces new uncertainty relations linking chirality and energy.

title: Hypercomplex Yang-Mills Theory as a Bipartite Gauge Field Model
summary: A non-Abelian gauge field framework is proposed using the hypercomplex ring formalism. This extension generates non-compact hyperbolic symmetries, which, alongside the compact gauge symmetries, double the internal degrees of freedom. This will enable the description of bipartite gauge systems and demonstrate how field dissipation operates at the dynamical level. Working within a commutative ring allows for the decoupling of the algebraic structures and facilitates the construction of solutions to the equations of motion.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a non-Abelian gauge field framework using hypercomplex rings, generating non-compact hyperbolic symmetries alongside compact gauge symmetries to double internal degrees of freedom. This enables bipartite gauge systems and dynamical field dissipation, with the commutative ring structure simplifying solution construction.
AI.motivation: To extend gauge field theory by incorporating non-compact hyperbolic symmetries via hypercomplex rings, enabling the description of bipartite gauge systems and field dissipation at the dynamical level.
AI.method: A hypercomplex ring formalism is introduced where a commutative ring structure decouples algebraic components, allowing non-compact hyperbolic symmetries to coexist with compact gauge symmetries, doubling the internal degrees of freedom.
AI.result: The framework successfully describes bipartite gauge systems and demonstrates how field dissipation operates dynamically, with the commutative ring facilitating solution construction.
AI.conclusion: The hypercomplex ring approach provides a novel algebraic structure for non-Abelian gauge theories that naturally incorporates both compact and non-compact symmetries, offering new tools for analyzing dissipative gauge systems.

title: Thermodynamics in symmetry-improved Cornwall-Jackiw-Tomboulis formalism: application to the low-energy effective theory of QCD
summary: We study the thermodynamics of the symmetry-improved Cornwall-Jackiw-Tomboulis (SICJT) formalism and apply it to a low-energy effective theory of QCD. In the symmetry-improved formulation, Ward-Takahashi identities are restored by auxiliary sources whose values are fixed self-consistently by the equilibrium state. While this construction improves the symmetry properties of the loop-wise truncated two-particle-irreducible (2PI) theory, it also makes the thermodynamic interpretation of the pressure nontrivial. We formulate several pressure prescriptions, including the conventional vacuum-subtracted pressure, a source-matched subtraction, and a pulled-back pressure in which the explicit source-induced energy shift is removed. Using the three-flavor linear sigma model with quarks, we analyze the equation of state, isentropic trajectories, adiabatic sound velocity, and trace anomaly across the chiral transition. We find that the global thermodynamic structure is stable under the different prescriptions, while quantitative differences are concentrated near the crossover and first-order transition region. These results establish a practical framework for constructing thermodynamically consistent observables in symmetry-improved 2PI approaches.

AI.tldr: The paper studies thermodynamics in the symmetry-improved Cornwall-Jackiw-Tomboulis (SICJT) formalism applied to low-energy QCD, proposing several pressure prescriptions (vacuum-subtracted, source-matched, pulled-back) and analyzing the equation of state, isentropic trajectories, sound velocity, and trace anomaly across the chiral transition using a three-flavor linear sigma model with quarks. The global thermodynamic structure is stable, with quantitative differences near crossover/first-order transitions.
AI.motivation: The symmetry-improved 2PI formalism restores Ward-Takahashi identities but makes thermodynamic interpretation of pressure nontrivial; the paper aims to establish a practical framework for constructing thermodynamically consistent observables in such approaches.
AI.method: The authors formulate three pressure prescriptions (conventional vacuum-subtracted, source-matched subtraction, and pulled-back pressure removing explicit source-induced energy shift), then apply these to a three-flavor linear sigma model with quarks, analyzing equation of state, isentropic trajectories, adiabatic sound velocity, and trace anomaly across the chiral transition.
AI.result: Global thermodynamic structure remains stable under different pressure prescriptions, while quantitative differences are concentrated near the crossover and first-order transition region.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a practical framework for constructing thermodynamically consistent observables in symmetry-improved 2PI approaches.

title: Magic Relations and Critical Varieties of Feynman Integrals
summary: Magic relations are a class of integration-by-parts identities where all integrals in the generating sector drop out. Since their presence causes several otherwise successful methods in the Feynman-integral computational pipeline to break down, they are important to detect and understand. In this paper, we take a first step toward a systematic characterization of such identities. Specifically, we observe and argue that the occurrence of magic relations always coincides with the presence of higher-dimensional critical varieties in the generating sector. This provides a practical computational test to check if a family of Feynman integrals can contain magic relations and to find them, which we implement in the ancillary Mathematica file Magic-Test.m. Additionally, we discuss how to count the number of master integrals in the presence of higher-dimensional critical varieties, classify the behavior of magic relations under symmetries, and we discuss their interplay with cuts.

AI.tldr: Magic relations in Feynman integrals are characterized by higher-dimensional critical varieties in the generating sector, enabling a practical test for their detection and classification.
AI.motivation: Magic relations cause breakdowns in several successful methods for Feynman-integral computation, making it important to detect and understand them systematically.
AI.method: The paper observes and argues that magic relations coincide with higher-dimensional critical varieties in the generating sector, and implements a computational test (Magic-Test.m) to detect them.
AI.result: A practical computational test is provided to check if a family of Feynman integrals can contain magic relations; the number of master integrals in the presence of higher-dimensional critical varieties is discussed.
AI.conclusion: Magic relations are linked to higher-dimensional critical varieties, enabling systematic detection; the work also classifies magic relations under symmetries and studies their interplay with cuts.

title: HyperPrecision: A Mathematica package for High-Precision Numerical Evaluation of Multivariate Hypergeometric Functions
summary: In this paper, we present HyperPrecision, a Mathematica package for high-precision numerical evaluation of general Horn-type multivariate hypergeometric functions and their Laurent expansions in a small parameter $ε$. Such functions appear widely in physics and mathematics, with applications ranging from quantum field theory and string theory to number theory and statistics. Their high-precision numerical evaluation, however, remains challenging, since their defining series converge only in restricted domains and analytic continuation beyond these domains is, in general, non-trivial. HyperPrecision addresses this problem by automatically constructing the Pfaffian system of partial differential equations for a given hypergeometric function and restricting it to a one-dimensional contour in the space of variables connecting the starting to the target point. The resulting ordinary differential equation is then solved by the Frobenius method, with boundary conditions fixed analytically by the defining series. We illustrate the use of the package by evaluating commonly occurring multivariate hypergeometric functions, including the Appell $F_1$, $F_2$, $F_3$, and $F_4$ functions, the Horn $G$- and $H$-series, and the Lauricella $F_A$, $F_B$, $F_C$, and $F_D$ functions, as well as by considering applications to angular integrals, Feynman integrals, and cosmological and holographic correlators.

AI.tldr: HyperPrecision is a Mathematica package for high-precision numerical evaluation of Horn-type multivariate hypergeometric functions and their Laurent expansions in ε, using automatic Pfaffian system construction and Frobenius method along one-dimensional contours.
AI.motivation: High-precision numerical evaluation of multivariate hypergeometric functions is challenging because their defining series converge only in restricted domains, and analytic continuation beyond these domains is generally non-trivial.
AI.method: The package automatically constructs the Pfaffian system of PDEs for a given hypergeometric function, restricts it to a one-dimensional contour in variable space, solves the resulting ODE via the Frobenius method, and fixes boundary conditions analytically using the defining series.
AI.result: Demonstrated evaluation of Appell F1-F4, Horn G- and H-series, Lauricella FA-FD functions, and applications to angular integrals, Feynman integrals, cosmological and holographic correlators.
AI.conclusion: HyperPrecision enables reliable high-precision evaluation and Laurent expansion of multivariate hypergeometric functions, with broad applicability across quantum field theory, string theory, number theory, and statistics.

title: Five-dimensional Geometry from Spinning Amplitudes
summary: Massive spinor-helicity variables in four dimensions are a useful tool for studying amplitudes between higher-spin fields and gravitons. Among them a special, simple set of amplitudes reproduces the linearized stress-energy tensor of a Kerr black hole in the classical limit. In this work we initiate the study of the classical limit of three-point spinor-helicity amplitudes in five dimensions. We introduce the map between the spinor invariants and the expectation values of spin operators and match the amplitude building blocks with those of the multipole expansion. Interestingly, in order to take the classical limit of a general amplitude, we need to augment the multipole structures with the Hodge dual of the classical spin tensor. We study the classical limit of alternative spinning states not described by fully-symmetric products of polarisations and conclude that they can describe the same spacetimes. Finally, by relaxing the orthogonality condition of the spin tensor we are able to model spacetimes with a single rotational isometry and match these to the classical limit of amplitudes allowing for an internal spin shift. Along the way we also identify the class of amplitudes describing the Myers-Perry black hole and comment on its generalization to arbitrary dimensions.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the study of classical limits of spinor-helicity amplitudes from four to five dimensions, connecting amplitude building blocks to multipole expansions and describing spinning black hole spacetimes including Myers-Perry black holes.
AI.motivation: To initiate the study of the classical limit of three-point spinor-helicity amplitudes in five dimensions, extending the successful four-dimensional framework that connects amplitudes to Kerr black hole stress-energy tensors.
AI.method: The authors introduce a map between spinor invariants and expectation values of spin operators, match amplitude building blocks with multipole expansion structures, augment multipole structures with the Hodge dual of the classical spin tensor, relax orthogonality conditions for spin tensors, and identify amplitude classes describing Myers-Perry black holes.
AI.result: A general classical limit of five-dimensional amplitudes requires augmenting multipole structures with the Hodge dual of the classical spin tensor. Alternative spinning states (not fully-symmetric polarisation products) can describe the same spacetimes. Relaxing spin tensor orthogonality allows modeling spacetimes with single rotational isometry. Amplitudes describing the Myers-Perry black hole are identified.
AI.conclusion: The five-dimensional classical limit framework for spinor-helicity amplitudes successfully connects to multipole expansions and black hole spacetimes, with generalizations to arbitrary dimensions noted.

title: On the Validity of the Effective Theory of (Multi-)Field Inflation
summary: Motivated by trans-Planckian issues in inflation, we determine the Hilbert space and amplitudes of quantum perturbations in the general low-energy effective theory of (multi-)field inflation without relying on the sub-horizon limit. The scalar sector is the most intricate, featuring field mixings and second-class constraints, which we handle using Dirac brackets. These results enable us to estimate the magnitude of higher-derivative corrections. In the specific case of slow-roll inflation, such estimate can be expressed in terms of the first slow-roll parameter $ε$ for a given cutoff $Λ$. We apply our results to several inflationary models with finite $Λ$: Higgs inflation, the Starobinsky model, natural inflation and hilltop inflation.

AI.tldr: Determines the Hilbert space and amplitudes of quantum perturbations in the general low-energy effective theory of (multi-)field inflation using Dirac brackets to handle scalar field mixings and second-class constraints, bypassing the sub-horizon limit. Estimates higher-derivative corrections and applies results to Higgs inflation, Starobinsky model, natural inflation, and hilltop inflation with finite cutoff Λ.
AI.motivation: To address trans-Planckian issues in inflation by determining the quantum structure of perturbations in the low-energy effective theory without relying on the sub-horizon limit, enabling estimation of higher-derivative corrections.
AI.method: Uses Dirac brackets to handle second-class constraints and field mixings in the scalar sector of multi-field inflation, constructing the Hilbert space and amplitudes of quantum perturbations within a general low-energy effective field theory framework.
AI.result: Provides an estimate of higher-derivative corrections magnitudes; for slow-roll inflation, expressed in terms of the first slow-roll parameter ε for a given cutoff Λ. Applied to Higgs inflation, Starobinsky model, natural inflation, and hilltop inflation.
AI.conclusion: A systematic effective field theory approach to quantum perturbations in inflation can circumvent sub-horizon limit assumptions and quantify trans-Planckian corrections across multiple inflationary models with a finite cutoff.

title: Black Hole Photon Rings Saturate the Quantum Chaos Bound
summary: We study the quantum chaos bound in the photon ring region surrounding black holes. By evaluating the Lyapunov exponent associated with unstable null geodesics in a broad class of generalized Kerr geometries, as well as the temperature induced by a string probe, we show that the quantum chaos bound is exactly saturated on equatorial circular orbits of the photon ring. We confirm our result by deriving the same exponent from out-of-time-order correlators in the near ring region. As a byproduct, we show that the photon ring saturation of the quantum chaos bound implies the saturation of the Bekenstein bound on the rate of information emission from the ringdown phase through the quasi-normal modes in the eikonal limit. Our results extend the known correspondence between black hole thermodynamics and chaotic dynamics, highlighting the role of the photon ring as a probe of the fundamental limits on thermalization and information scrambling in black holes.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates the quantum chaos bound in the photon ring of black holes, showing it is exactly saturated on equatorial circular orbits, and connects this saturation to the Bekenstein bound on information emission during the ringdown phase.
AI.motivation: To understand the fundamental limits of quantum chaos and information scrambling in black hole spacetimes, specifically in the photon ring region, and to explore connections between black hole thermodynamics, chaotic dynamics, and information bounds.
AI.method: Evaluating Lyapunov exponents from unstable null geodesics in generalized Kerr geometries and temperatures from string probes; deriving exponents from out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) in the near-ring region.
AI.result: The quantum chaos bound is exactly saturated on equatorial circular orbits of the photon ring; the photon ring saturation also implies saturation of the Bekenstein bound on information emission rate from ringdown quasi-normal modes in the eikonal limit.
AI.conclusion: The findings extend the correspondence between black hole thermodynamics and chaotic dynamics, highlighting the photon ring as a key probe of fundamental limits on thermalization and information scrambling in black holes.

title: Perturbative Nicolai-Map Diagrammatics: Application to Poincaré Supergravity
summary: We develop a perturbative, diagrammatic framework for constructing Nicolai maps and apply it to four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ Poincaré supergravity expanded around flat Minkowski space. It provides an alternative to the coupling-flow-operator construction, which faces several obstructions when extended to local supersymmetry. Expanding the bosonic effective action and the Nicolai map jointly in the gravitational coupling $κ$ and the loop-counting parameter $\hbar$, we derive the Nicolai-map defining conditions, i.e. the free-action and determinant-matching conditions, order by order. The diagrammatics enumerates all admissible local terms in the Nicolai-map ansatz from the effective-action diagrams and reduces the construction to a finite system of nonlinear polynomial equations. Carried through order $κ^{2}$, the resulting constraints are found to be independent of the detailed bosonic input and hierarchical, order-$κ^{2}$ consistency further restricting the order-$κ$ data. A consistent Nicolai-map construction for the Einstein--Hilbert graviton sector is found to require the Rarita--Schwinger gravitino already at this order: Einstein gravity admits a Nicolai map only through its $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetric completion, Poincaré supergravity, supporting Nicolai's characterization of supersymmetry.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a perturbative diagrammatic framework for constructing Nicolai maps and applies it to 4D $\mathcal{N}=1$ Poincaré supergravity. The construction reveals that Einstein gravity alone cannot admit a Nicolai map—it requires the full $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetric completion (Poincaré supergravity) to be consistent, thereby supporting Nicolai's characterization of supersymmetry.
AI.motivation: To overcome obstructions faced by the coupling-flow-operator construction when extending Nicolai maps to local supersymmetry, and to systematically derive the defining conditions for Nicolai maps in supergravity.
